narrative.overview: The user-selected visual world combines a public exhibition's legibility with technical diagrams that can actually be inspected. It uses generous light reading fields, dark system panels and a restrained green emphasis. It is neither a campaign poster nor an official government interface.
keyCharacteristics: Strong, clean typography with spacious editorial pacing.
Flat surfaces and precise geometric routing lines.
Evidence notes, interactive states and clear uncertainty boundaries.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: Colour identifies visual roles, never the truth or falsity of a claim by itself.

rules.name: The Legibility Rule
rules.body: Keep heading tracking at or above -0.04em; reduce scale before allowing text to collide with a diagram boundary.

dos: Do retain visible focus, native keyboard operation and reduced-motion behavior.
Do label conceptual diagrams and distinguish statements, analysis and recommendations.
Do keep typography and controls within the existing forest/paper/lime system.
donts: Don't turn institutional claims into assertions that the software has been independently verified.
Don't imply that source publication exposes voter records or credentials.
Don't add ornamental cards, glass effects, fake terminal output or photos to replace explanatory geometry.
